extracted.intended_audience: prospective SFF grant applicants and SFF Speculators (individual expedited funders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for requesting and administering SFF Speculation Grants: how to apply, expected timelines, how grants affect later S-Process evaluations, and how Speculators' budgets are adjusted via impact futures settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request a Speculation Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a Speculation Grant, complete and submit the SFF Funding Rolling Application. Filling out this application submits a Speculation Grant Request for expedited funding as well as a request for consideration in the next S-Process Grant Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting by the S-Process Grant Round deadline is required for Speculators to settle a Speculation Grant to you in the upcoming round; chances improve by submitting early. You can still apply even if there is no currently open grant round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timing and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed timeframe for decisions. A Speculation Grant could be made as quickly as one week after the grant request, as late as 14 days after the Grant Round application deadline (if a Speculator waits to see round applicants), or possibly even later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculators are individually free to reach out and make grants; timelines therefore vary by Speculator and logistical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information requirement for faster funding
rubrics_metrics.description: To get money faster, you have to provide more information, not less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You still have to submit a full application, to be evaluated by the S-Process Grant Round after the fact of the grant. Providing fuller information increases the likelihood/timeliness of receiving a Speculation Grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application required and post-hoc evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you receive a Speculation Grant for $Y from SFF, you must submit a full application; the grant will be evaluated by the S-Process Grant Round after the fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the S-Process recommends a total of $Z in the round, the $Y already given is counted against that total (see the 'grant deduction' rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant deduction against later S-Process recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive a Speculation Grant of $Y and the S-Process Grant Round later recommends your organization receive $Z, then the $Y is counted against the total $Z recommendation: SFF will recommend an additional max(0, $Z - $Y) after the close of the round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From a myopic perspective this guarantees at least $Y total, but can hurt reputation if the S-Process evaluates the grant poorly, or boost reputation if evaluated positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate uses of Speculation Grants (intended purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculation Grants can be intended for grants that are somewhat time sensitive and cannot wait for a few months until the next SFF round distributes grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently all Speculation Grants are funded by donations from Jaan Tallinn and can be intended for funding requests that can’t wait to be processed by the most recently announced S-Process Grant Round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculator budgets and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Speculator has a limited budget for approving Speculation Grants (typically $400k; average around $500k), from which to approve grants. A Speculator's budget is an internal spreadsheet entry representing planned listening to their suggestions; the person does not receive money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Speculator makes a grant, the amount is subtracted from their budget so they can recommend less until their budget is adjusted by impact future settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculator behavior and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Speculator is individually free to make Speculation Grants, though they are expected to notify the other Speculators of their decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculators choose how and what to prioritize (e.g., make high-value grants to grow budget, or fund things unlikely to be valued by the S-Process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of grant deduction and impact future when grant is made
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Speculation Grant is recommended and made (e.g., $50k), three things are recorded: the Speculator’s budget is reduced by $50k; a grant deduction of $50k to the recipient is recorded in the S-Process recommendation process (so the next S-Process recommendation will subtract that $50k); and an impact future for the grant is recorded for the Speculator’s grant-making budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant deduction is marked 'settled' when the S-Process later grants are disbursed and does not carry forward; the impact future is used to adjust the Speculator's budget according to a later settlement calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact futures settlement principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Speculation Grant creates an impact future (certificate) that 'settles' by adjusting the Speculator's budget according to an evaluation performed in the next S-Process Grant Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement value is the product of the utility value of the grant as evaluated by Jaan’s delegates in the next S-Process round and a normalization factor chosen so the total settlement budget matches Jaan’s chosen budget for settling certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: How 'fd_value' (first-dollar value) is calculated
rubrics_metrics.description: fd_value(cert) = the total dollar value of the first 50k Jaan-dollars recommended for the recipient, as calculated by the S-Process simulator with the cert’s Speculator recused, other Funders removed, and no discount/hold options. fd_value is some number less than 50k and is proportional to the certificate’s value in 'first dollars'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simulator defines the most valuable Jaan-funded dollar as valued at $1, renormalizes and caps first-dollar values at 1, and computes fd_value for the certificate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement normalization and final settlement_value formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement proceeds by summing fd_value(cert) across all certificates to get total_fd_value; Jaan chooses a settlement_budget; settlement_normalizer = settlement_budget / total_fd_value; then settlement_value(cert) = fd_value(cert) * settlement_normalizer; the Speculator's budget is adjusted by adding settlement_value(cert) (after subtracting the original grant amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If settlement_budget is greater than the total amount granted through Speculation Grants, the program grows; otherwise it shrinks. Jaan may delegate choosing settlement_budget to the S-Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal in evaluation of impact futures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Speculator is also serving as a grant Recommender for the S-Process, they are 'recused' such that their values are purged from the system during the evaluation of their own future certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recusal ensures that fd_value and settlement calculations exclude the Speculator’s own influence on the evaluation of the grant they recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and funding channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculation Grants are primarily administered through SFF's DAF, funded via donations from Jaan Tallinn. Some Speculation Grants (e.g., to for-profit organizations) are administered through Survival and Flourishing Corp and also funded by Jaan Tallinn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the future additional S-Process Funders might join; administrative path affects how grants are processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic implication for Speculators (how to grow budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Speculator's best strategy to grow their Speculation Grant budget is to make grants that the next S-Process Grant Round will consider to be highly valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculators may also choose to fund things unlikely to be valued by the S-Process; the choice affects their future budget via settlement.
